page.title: Structured Data
page.hint: Add to or override the structured data a page already provides for search engines. Fill it per page type and save per language; leave it empty to keep the original. Brand, address and phone are maintained in Page Info and Language Content, so there is no need to repeat them here.

card.help-hint: Paste a JSON object, an array of objects, or a whole JSON block with @graph. Item 1 of the array rewrites entry 1 of the page structured data and only the properties you write are replaced; extra items are added. An object with @type matches by type, with @id matches by id. Empty objects {} are skipped, null removes a property, and keys next to @graph are merged into the outermost level.

status.empty: Not set: nothing changes; the page keeps its original data.
status.merge: Merged into the existing %s; added automatically when the type is missing.
status.position: No @type: matched by position — item 1 rewrites entry 1, item 2 rewrites entry 2 and so on; extra items are added and empty objects {} are skipped.
status.root: Another %d item(s) alongside @graph are merged into the outermost level.
status.error: Invalid format (%s). The front end ignores this block.

page.title: Monitoring
page.hint: Clarity and gtag settings, plus which event fires when. The front-end script only reads this configuration, so no ID is hardcoded any more.

card.switch-hint: This site, cookie consent and site SEO are independent switches; combine them as needed. Which tracking scripts load is decided only by the Clarity and Google switches below.
card.clarity-hint: Clarity only records sessions and heatmaps. It does not use gtag, has no conversions and sends no custom events, so it is configured on its own.
card.google-hint: The GA4 property, Google Ads, Google Tag and Tag Manager containers all share the same gtag configuration: the page loads gtag.js once, then calls gtag('config', id) for each ID below. No conversion label is needed here.
card.event-hint: Each event has one type: GA4 record sends the event name; Ads conversion sends conversion with the Google Ads send_to value. Pick "Default" as the source to cover every source; an exact source wins.

notice.expired: The page expired. Please save again.

monitor.gtag-empty: No gtag configuration yet. Use "Add config" below to start.
monitor.event-empty: No event sending yet. Use "Add event" below to start.

hint.clarity-id: The project ID from Clarity under Settings → Overview, ten letters and digits.
hint.gtag: One ID per row; the page calls gtag('config', id) for each of them. G- is a GA4 property, AW- is Google Ads, GT- is a Google tag and GTM- is a Tag Manager container (the container loads gtm.js separately and its events are configured in Tag Manager). Conversion labels belong to Event sending, not here.
hint.event: A GA4 record sends the event name (for example generate_lead); an Ads conversion always sends conversion with the Google Ads send_to value, for example AW-XXXXXXXXXX/XXXXXXXXXX.
hint.savebar: Takes effect immediately after saving; no asset rebuild needed.
hint.site: With Clarity or Google tracking enabled, turning this switch off means only visitors coming through the CDN are tracked; direct traffic to the origin (including local debugging) is ignored.
hint.consent: Off = consent assumed, scripts load with the page. On = the cookie notice appears first and scripts load only after the visitor agrees.
hint.seo: When off, the origin outputs noindex, follow and robots.txt becomes Disallow: /; requests through the CDN are still crawlable, so the live site keeps its indexing.
hint.clarity-on: When off, the Clarity script is not loaded and no sessions or heatmaps are recorded.
hint.google-on: When off, none of the gtag configurations loads. The IDs are kept and come back when switched on again.
